analyst_view.overall: Werder Bremen (6th, 18 points) host bottom side Gladbach (4 points from 10) on Friday night. Daniel Thioune, who just signed a contract extension, saw Werder beat Hamburg 4-0 in the Nordderby; right-back Mitchell Weiser trained again on Monday and Thioune expects him to be available, Marco Grüll (calf) could return from the bench at most, and Felix Agu is only partly back in training and too early for this game. Alexander Blessin's Gladbach have Tim Kleindienst and Hugo Bolin back in team training, but Blessin says he will not rush them before the midweek cup tie at Darmstadt, and Robin Hack missed Monday's training with a muscle problem. The numbers already take off Weiser, Bolin and Ullrich and add for Werder's strong recent shooting and Gladbach's rise in bookings; the possible returns and Hack's doubt roughly cancel out and no referee is named yet, so I stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.9 for Werder. They already take off Weiser for Werder and Bolin and Ullrich for Gladbach; Weiser looks likely to play and Bolin or Kleindienst may make the bench, which would add a little, but Hack's muscle problem pulls the other way. I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 5.4 for Werder. Weiser's likely return gives Werder their usual width on the right, while Agu is still out on the left; Gladbach have conceded more corners than usual lately, which the numbers already add. I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Gladbach have picked up 20 cards in their last six, a sign of a side fighting at the bottom, and the numbers already add about 8% for it; no referee has been named yet and there is no derby edge. I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, 18.3 for Werder. Werder's 105 shots in six are already counted with an 11% boost, and Gladbach's attack has been without Kleindienst since September, which their form shows. I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, 7.0 for Werder. Werder's sharp recent finishing, with Njinmah scoring twice against Hamburg, is already counted, and Gladbach's thin attack is in their form. I stay at about 11.2.
